contract.intent: Define and lock the flow-control semantics — the common workflow skeleton (node creation, completion, chain append) plus per-work-type flows and the input-resolution ladder. This is the contract the planner kernel (S5) implements; all other slices run under it.
acceptanceCriteria: Common skeleton documented: lifecycle (spawn → materialize → validate → activate → execute → verify → commit), gates (round, artifact, completion), statuses (queued/active/blocked/done/failed/superseded)

HUMAN GATES at each end of every step: entry gate = grilling (human validates understanding/approach before execution); exit gate = confirm-result (human confirms the step's output before commit). Each step STOPS and waits for human input at both gates

Rejection semantics: when the human rejects at either gate, the step reworks based on its artifacts + the recorded feedback — bounded (max iterations, checkpoint preserved, fallback); rejected attempts preserved via events, rework = sibling-correction

Human-interface adapter contract (pluggable): basic = talk (round-and-round conversation); other forms (e.g., interactive HTML) supported via plugins; the adapter handles present-draft / collect-decision / collect-feedback / present-question / collect-answer

Node/nodeGroup creation + chain-append rules: planner-only creation, sibling-correction retries, parallel groups, round N+1 only after round N's completed event, requiredInputs = previous rounds'/steps' artifacts
Completion semantics: ACs verified + evidence + artifact gate + human confirmation; done/failed/superseded
Input-resolution ladder integrated at materialize: derive → probe → infer (labeled, forbidden on high-impact/no-fallback) → ask (batched, deduped) → block — per the silent-inference rule (design §8)
Per-work-type flow definitions for v1 kinds: grilling, planning/expansion, implementation, binding, review (+ human mode) — common structure, varying flow
Flow-control spec locked (upstream design §6/§21, ann-spec, tree-format-spec-v2); S5 planner kernel cites it
